fieldValues.title: May the arrangement fixture add two container-literal Compositions to the allowlist?
fieldValues.decision_question: May scripts/composition-container-literal-allowlist.json gain two entries so the arrangement conformance fixture can test rule flattening [R8] and supplied-versus-literal container precedence [R9]?
fieldValues.context:
Problem: The RFC-043 arrangement conformance fixture cannot test two rules (a rule section flattening a nested container, and a supplied container overriding a differing literal) without a Composition that names a Container by id, and the check that forbids that (check-composition-container-literal.mjs, RFC-043 ruling M, srs#851) only allows listed exceptions.
Why it matters: Without these scenarios a third-party renderer and the reference implementation can disagree on which container wins and on how a rule section lays out nested entries, and both claim conformance. That is the drift SP-01 names. The allowlist is the owner's ruled, shrinking exception; adding to it touches a gate, which the third-party-ready group may not do on its own.
Options and consequences: (1) Add two allowlist entries citing srs#977: both scenarios land now, the allowlist grows by two until srs#851 removes it. (2) Create the Composition at run time inside the scenario: no allowlist change, but the runner needs a new create-then-render operation and scenarios.json still carries the literal, which the same check scans. (3) Do nothing: the clauses stay listed as not covered.
Recommendation: Option 1, two entries, each citing srs#977 and removed with the rest by srs#851.
Action needed: decide
Urgency: low; srs#977 is otherwise delivered in srs PR #980.
Answers: SP-01 "Spec, schema and tool keep drifting apart"
fieldValues.friction: srs#977 asks for these scenarios from RFC-043's own conformance list, but the only way to express them trips a gate the group cannot change. Needs deciding now because srs PR #980 ships the rest and the README lists these two as not covered.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: 1. Add two allowlist entries (srs#977). 2. Create the Composition inside the scenario at run time (new runner operation, literal still scanned). 3. Do nothing, leave the two clauses uncovered.
fieldValues.key_requirements: The allowlist keeps shrinking toward srs#851; new entries are tied to a live issue; no scenario that a runner cannot drive; expectations captured from the pinned CLI.
fieldValues.decision_statement: Add two allowlist entries, one per Composition (outline-view-rule, outline-view-literal), each citing srs#977, then add the [R8] and [R9] scenarios.
fieldValues.rationale: The allowlist is the owner's ruled exception mechanism for exactly this and expires with srs#851; the scenarios close a real conformance gap.
fieldValues.revisit_when: srs#851 lands and removes the literals and the allowlist file.
fieldValues.next_steps: If approved: the builder adds the entries and scenarios in a follow-up PR on srs#977 and checks the runner handles the keys.
